response.sql: WITH cat AS (SELECT category, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining, SUM(amount - spent) AS total FROM budget WHERE amount > 75 GROUP BY category), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM cat) SELECT cat.category, cat.avg_remaining, cat.total, cat.total - overall.avg_total AS diff_above_avg FROM cat CROSS JOIN overall WHERE overall.avg_total IS NOT NULL AND cat.total > overall.avg_total

assumptions.assumption: Categories with a NULL total (no non-null amount-spent values) are kept in the grouping but are ignored by the overall AVG, as AVG skips NULLs; they cannot exceed the average so they are not listed.
NULL category values form their own group, as in a plain GROUP BY.
SUM(amount - spent) skips rows where either amount or spent is NULL, since the difference is NULL for those rows.
